column4: The section makes a furnished garden room the pattern for a furnished world; here Allah calls earth a bed, فِرَاشًا, and sky a building, بِنَاءً, stating that room and world relation directly.
The section's root reading of ر ف ع includes raising a building; Abraham and Ishmael raise the House's foundations, showing the same upward building action at human scale.

The section's dictionary image makes the raised sky a tent canopy whose pole is absent; this ayah says the heavens were raised بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا, letting the roof stand without visible supports.
Allah spreads the earth and sets firm mountains and rivers in it; the floor and upright mountain arrangement matches the section's world furnishing.
Earth is spread, mountains set firmly, and balanced growth brought forth there; this gives the section's level floor and planted supports a productive landscape.
The verse says mountains were set in the earth so it would not sway; this makes the section's mountain-as-peg image explain the world's stability.
In this garden, people recline on couches amid silk and ornaments; it turns the section's listed couches into an inhabited paradise setting.
Allah makes earth a cradle, مَهْدًا, and lays out paths in it; this presents the section's spread floor as a fitted place for human travel.
Firm mountains are placed so the earth will not shake with its inhabitants; the verse supplies the stabilizing purpose behind the section's upright mountains.
The section's dictionary describes the sky as a roof; here it is made a protected roof, سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا, directly turning that secondary sense into a cosmic image.
The section's root reading of ر ف ع includes raising buildings; this ayah uses تُرْفَعَ for houses set apart for remembrance, a human-scale instance of the same raised structure.
The section's root reading of ب ث ث links carpets spread out with creatures spread through the land; this ayah also places anchored mountains and a pillarless sky around that dispersed life.
People and their spouses recline on couches in the garden; this shows the section's couches as part of a social, lived-in room.
The people in this garden sit عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ, on couches facing one another; it adds the companionship and orientation that make the section's furniture a setting.
Allah makes earth a place of rest and sky a building, then shapes people well and provides good things; this gathers the section's floor, roof, and fitted creation into one account.
The verse sets mountains above the earth and apportions its provisions in measured days; it joins the section's planted landscape to its claim that making is measured.
The section's root reading of ب ث ث joins spread rugs to spread creatures; this ayah says creatures are dispersed through heavens and earth, making the world floor part of a populated design.
Allah makes earth a cradle, مَهْدًا, and puts paths through it; this is another direct picture of the earth as a fitted surface.
Golden trays and cups are circulated among the people of the garden; the placed cups of the section become part of an active feast.
The question أَفَلَمْ يَنظُرُوا invites people to look at the built and adorned sky above them; it echoes the section's call to inspect how the sky is raised.
Allah spreads the earth and casts firm mountains into it; this closely repeats the section's ground-and-mountain construction image.
The sky is built and made vast, بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ; this gives the section's raised canopy an explicit act of cosmic building.
The section's root reading for the spread carpet is echoed in Allah's words وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَاهَا; the earth itself is laid out as a floor covering.
The verse swears by the raised roof, السَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ; the section's dictionary sense of sky as a roof becomes a direct Qur'anic image.
The section's root ص ف ف describes cushions aligned in a straight row; here the garden's couches are مَصْفُوفَةً, giving the same ordered furniture arrangement.
The section's dictionary reading connects creation with correct measure; this ayah says every thing was created بِقَدَرٍ, making measured workmanship explicit.
The section calls attention to lifting and placing; here Allah raises the sky and places the balance, رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ, joining those actions in one created order.
The section's root reading of وَضَعَ includes setting an object in place; this ayah says Allah placed the earth for all creatures, وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ.
Garden dwellers recline on richly lined couches with fruit close at hand; this gives the section's furnishings their setting and use.
The section names cushions and rugs as furnishings; this garden has green cushions, رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ, and fine carpets, عَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسَانٍ, a direct furnishing parallel.
The verse names raised couches, فُرُشٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ; it matches the section's root ر ف ع and its lifted garden furniture.
The section's image of the earth as a spread covering is stated here as Allah making the earth بِسَاطًا, a carpet or broad spread.
The earth is made a bed, مِهَادًا; this is a direct counterpart to the section's level, laid-out world.
The mountains are made pegs, أَوْتَادًا; this directly names the same support image the section develops for mountains in the earth.
The sky above is built as seven strong structures; it extends the section's raised world canopy into a constructed ceiling.
The verse says the sky's height was raised and then proportioned, رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا; it directly joins the section's lifting and measured shaping.
The section's dictionary reading of خَلَقَ includes measuring material to fit; here Allah says He created, proportioned, and balanced the human form, خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ.
The section cites this wording, خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ, as creation followed by setting in order; it gives the room and world parallel a compact Qur'anic formulation.
The section's root reading of ب ث ث links a spread carpet with living things spread on earth; this verse says Allah dispersed every kind of creature there, making the laid-out world inhabited.
The section's dictionary reading of creation as measured workmanship meets this ayah's بِقَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ, a known measure for what is sent down.
The section places the camel beside cushions aligned in a row; here sacrificial camels stand صَوَافَّ, joining its animal and alignment images while adding the distinct setting of sacrifice.
The section's dictionary entry gives measuring as a secondary sense of خَلَقَ; this ayah says Allah created all things and determined them precisely, فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا.
The section's root reading of ب ث ث links a spread surface with dispersed creatures; here rain revives earth and Allah disperses creatures through the two realms.
Allah holds the heavens and earth lest they slip away; this adds the sustaining force behind the section's roof-and-floor world.
The section's root ص ف ف describes placing things in a straight line; this oath pictures beings lined up in ranks, وَالصَّافَّاتِ صَفًّا.
The section's cups are placed in a furnished garden; this neighboring ayah to 37:44 shows a cup from a flowing spring being circulated among those seated there.
The heavens are completed as seven and the nearest sky adorned with lamps; this adds a decorated ceiling to the section's constructed cosmos.
The section's root reading of ب ث ث connects spread rugs and spread life; this verse calls human creation and the creatures Allah disperses signs to reflect on.
This ayah continues the balance placed in 55:7 by warning people not to transgress the scale; the section's measured craft thus opens onto the limits of human measure.
After the balance in 55:7 and warning in 55:8, this ayah orders just weight; it gives the section's measured order a human practice as well.
The section's dictionary image compares the world to a tent; this verse places garden companions in pavilions, الْخِيَامِ, a literal tent-like dwelling within paradise.
This garden's couches are woven or inlaid, سُرُرٍ مَوْضُونَةٍ; the detail expands the section's list of crafted furnishings.
The ayah continues the couches of 56:15 and seats their occupants facing each other; it adds a social arrangement to the section's ordered room.
The section's root ص ف ف describes things aligned in a straight row; this verse praises people standing in ranks like a compact structure, صَفًّا كَأَنَّهُم بُنْيَانٌ مَّرْصُوصٌ.
The sky is created in layers with no mismatch; this makes the section's raised ceiling a deliberately ordered construction.
After 67:3 describes the layered sky, this ayah tells the viewer to look again for flaws; it echoes the section's invitation to inspect the created world.
The sky is made in seven layers, طِبَاقًا; this supplies another image of a deliberately constructed canopy.
After 71:19 calls earth a carpet, this ayah says people travel along its broad roads; the spread surface is made usable for movement.
Garden dwellers recline on couches under protection from sun and cold; this situates couches as the section's sheltered room furnishings.
Silver vessels and cups are carried around to the garden dwellers; this is a direct counterpart to the section's placed cups.
The section names cups among measured furnishings; this verse says the cups are made to a measured size, قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا.
The section's root ص ف ف links furnishings to straight rows; here the Spirit and angels stand in ranks, صَفًّا, on the appointed day.
After 79:28 raises and proportions the sky, this ayah describes the earth spread out, دَحَاهَا, completing the paired roof-and-floor scene.
This ayah continues the proportioned form of 82:7 by saying Allah assembled a person in whichever form He willed; it extends the section's measured making to chosen shape.
The garden dwellers recline on couches and look out; this repeats the section's furniture in a setting of settled ease.
The righteous again sit on couches and look out; the repeated scene reinforces the couch as a feature of the garden setting.
After 87:2 says creation is set in order, this ayah says Allah measured and guided it, قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ; it makes the section's measure-before-fitting theme explicit.
The section's root ص ف ف describes ordered rows; here angels arrive rank upon rank, صَفًّا صَفًّا, on the Day of Judgment.
The oath names the sky and its builder; this echoes the section's sky as a constructed roof.
The oath names the earth and the One who spread it, طَحَاهَا; it repeats the section's image of a laid-out ground.
After sky-building and earth-spreading in 91:5–6, this ayah says the soul was proportioned, سَوَّاهَا; it extends the section's ordered creation theme to a living form.
The section presents mountains set in place and an exposed, spread earth; here mountains are made to move and earth is laid bare at gathering, reversing that settled landscape.
The section shows mountains erected as supports; here the Lord says He will blow them away, يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفًا, reversing their planted stability.
The section's source lexicon uses صَفْصَف for level land; after 20:105 removes the mountains, this ayah leaves a level plain, قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا, turning the pegs into bare floor.
This continues the level plain of 20:106, with no crookedness or unevenness; the emptied ground completes the reversal of the section's furnished, shaped world.
The section imagines the sky as a raised canopy; here the heavens are folded like a written scroll, a specific reversal of that stretched roof.
The section asks how mountains are set up; this verse says they seem fixed while they pass like clouds, exposing the boundary of that apparent stability.
The section's roof and mountains are settled structures; this Day of Judgment scene says the mountains move, unsettling the fitted landscape.
The section's earth is laid out as a stable floor; here earth is shaken violently, reversing its settled surface.
The section's mountains stand as placed supports; here they are crushed, بُسَّتِ الْجِبَالُ بَسًّا, and lose that form.
The section shows earth and mountains fitted into place; here both are lifted and crushed with one blow, reversing their construction.
The section's sky is a raised roof; here on the Day of Judgment the sky is like molten metal, a specific change of the overhead scene.
The section's source dictionary links earth-coverings with wool; here mountains are like carded wool, الْعِهْنِ, as their firm form unravels.
The section's mountains are planted supports; here earth and mountains shake and the mountains become shifting sand dunes, reversing that stability.
The section shows mountains set upright in the world's design; this Judgment scene says they are blown away.
The section's mountains are fixed and upright; here they are set moving until they become a mirage, سَرَابًا.
The section's mountain supports appear set in place; here the mountains are set in motion on the Day the created order is transformed.
The section treats earth as a spread floor; here the earth is stretched out at the Judgment, a boundary where its settled form changes.
The section presents earth as a fitted floor; here earth is pounded flat and pulverized, ending that stable arrangement.
The section's world has a level, laid-out earth; here the earth is shaken with its final convulsion, a direct reversal of the floor's stability.
After the shaking of 99:1, the earth casts out its burdens; this continues the rupture of the section's settled, furnishing surface.
The section's root reading of ب ث ث describes rugs spread out; here people are scattered like moths, الْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ, turning a laid-out covering into a dispersed Judgment scene.
The section's dictionary entry says a thick rug may be made of wool; here mountains become carded wool, الْعِهْنِ الْمَنفُوشِ, so the planted landscape unravels into textile-like matter.
